title: Which squares does a piece attack?
outcomes: Taps every square a rook, bishop, knight or pawn attacks when other pieces stand in the way
Stops a line at the first piece it meets and keeps the squares behind it out
Knows a pawn attacks diagonally ahead, even when blocked, and not straight ahead
Says a defended piece is still attacked

steps.text:
A piece **attacks** a square when it could capture an enemy piece standing there (pins aside; see the next card). If the square holds a piece of its own side, we say the piece **defends** it.
An attacked square need not hold anything yet. And the squares a piece attacks are not always the squares it moves to.

steps.caption: White to move. The lit squares are the squares the rook on e3 attacks.

claims.statement: These twelve squares are exactly the rook's attacked squares.
A black pawn stands on e7.
The rook can capture the pawn on e7.

steps.text:
A check before you trust 'attacks'.
**Lines:** a rook, bishop or queen attacks up to and including the first piece it meets. Squares behind it are not attacked until it leaves.
**Pawns:** two squares diagonally ahead, even when blocked; never the square straight ahead.
**Pinned pieces** still attack their squares. A defended piece is still attacked.
